chapter: Childhood, first teachers and the Wilberforce Collegians
title: Switching from BS to AB and telling his father at graduation
summary: Their father wanted a scientist son; Fletcher started as a chemist. Horace switched to an arts degree and only revealed it at graduation, then explained on a walk.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Yes. But I went to Wilberforce -- my father wanted one of his two sons to be a scientist, a bachelor of science. Fletcher started out that way.
He was a chemist, wasn't he?
A chemist, yeah. I meant chemist.

So he got to swinging, and he changed over. So my father said, 'Well, maybe my next son will do it, so why don't you go to Wilberforce.' He knew they had this there. I changed over from BS to bachelor of arts, and I didn't tell him about it, until the day of my graduation. And I'll never forget the look on his face when on graduation day, he was sitting right up front. He always had excellent ears, see, he could always hear. So when they handed me my diploma -- I had my gown on, my hat -- they said, 'Horace Henderson, AB.' I looked dead at my father, and he looked right at me, and he didn't say a word. We got through -- till the sermon was over and what-not (inaudible) -- exercise. He called me and we took a walk in the woods right at Wilberforce. We didn't say a word for about a half mile, and he stopped me and he put his hand on my shoulder, and he said, 'Son, how come?'

I knew. Then I had to go through misery and everything to explain to him why I did it and of course my only answer was that had I gone to bachelor of science I would have had to spent a lot of time in the laboratory, checking these unknowns, and (inaudible) these deals, and I

knew that I wouldn't have had the time for my music. So I said, "Father, I want to be a musician like my brother. He's succeeding with where he is on Broadway. I want to do this, and I know if I told you about it -- I wrote you about it, you wouldn't have agreed. So I had to take this chance." You know he took it beautiful, and you took about a relief --
I thought I would inject that. But this is --
